documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 10/07/2025

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Callahan returned for her yearly follow-up of papillary thyroid carcinoma, treated by total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection in 2019, and her postsurgical hypothyroidism.

She feels well. The palpitations, sweating and weight loss of last fall resolved within weeks and have not returned. She takes levothyroxine 112 mcg each morning and her calcium with vitamin D twice daily. No drug allergies.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Comfortable. Thyroid bed and lateral neck without mass or palpable lymph nodes. No tremor.

Labs today: TSH and free T4 within the reference range; thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL, undetectable.

Assessment: no clinical or biochemical evidence of disease. Replacement is adequate.

Plan: levothyroxine 112 mcg unchanged. Calcium/vitamin D unchanged. Return in one year with TSH, free T4 and thyroglobulin beforehand.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology Visit Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 03/30/2026

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Callahan on 03/30. Her roommate came with her and, with her permission, stayed for the visit.

She came in with anxiety, heavy sweating and swings in mood, which she says feel much like October 2024. Her roommate has noticed that she has become very focused on fitness lately and has been on strict diets and hard exercise routines. She has lost 8 lb in two months while her appetite has been good. When I asked about supplements she told me she has been buying 'metabolism boosters' online. She takes no prescription medicine apart from her levothyroxine.

Current medicines: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg / vitamin D3 400 IU twice daily; the online products. No drug allergies. Family history negative for thyroid disease.

Exam: pulse 102, BP 130/80. Alert and cooperative, visibly jittery. The thyroid bed is non-palpable, with no nodularity or tenderness.

We did labs and a radioiodine uptake. TSH <0.01, free T4 2.8 ng/dL, free T3 6.6 pg/mL, thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL. 24-hour uptake 0.5%.

Impression: recurrent thyrotoxicosis factitia. Undetectable thyroglobulin and negligible uptake again point to hormone from outside, and the online products are the likely source; products sold this way frequently contain thyroid hormone or thyroid extract.

Plan:
- Stop all of the online products now. She agreed.
- Levothyroxine 112 mcg unchanged.
- TSH and free T4 in 6 weeks, at your office as before.
- Her roommate's concern about her eating and exercise seemed worth passing on. I would be grateful if you could see her soon and follow up on it.
- Yearly surveillance visit in the fall as planned.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology
